name: Milk (Human) (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Milk (Human) [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 171279 (Milk, human, mature, fluid; SR Legacy NDB 01107) - full macronutrient, amino-acid, fatty-acid, vitamin, mineral panel
Soyyilmaz et al. 2021, Nutrients 13(8):2737 'The Mean of Milk: HMO concentrations throughout lactation' doi:10.3390/nu13082737
Nutrition During Lactation (IOM), NCBI Bookshelf NBK235590 - lactose 70 g/L, protein 8-9 g/L, minerals, taurine
van Sadelhoff et al. 2020, Nutrients (PMC7270293) - free amino acids: glutamate ~1.5 mM, glutamine ~0.6 mM
Faulkner & Peaker 1982, J Dairy Research - milk free glucose ~2 mM
Human-milk citrate literature (Holt 1993; casein-micelle studies) - citrate 2.1-2.8 mM
Paquette et al. 2023, PNAS 120 doi:10.1073/pnas.2221413120 - myo-inositol 14.9 mg/100 mL
Yamawaki et al. 1998 (PMID 9635064) - taurine ~300 umol/L in mature milk
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources for a microbial medium are LACTOSE (~200 mM) plus a large fermentable HMO pool (~11 g/L, uniquely human) and fat (~4.4 g/100 g); citrate (~2.5 mM) is the key organic acid the prior FooDB profile omitted. Protein is low (~1 g/100 g, whey-dominant) but supplemented by a rich free-amino-acid pool (glutamate/glutamine/taurine). The prior profile's 'sucrose' was corrected to lactose, and the plant furanocoumarin (R)-oxypeucedanin removed as FooDB noise.
curation_added: lactose (dominant carbon source, ~202 mM; was wrongly listed as sucrose)
citric acid / citrate (~2.5 mM) - the omitted organic acid
taurine (~0.30 mM free amino acid, absent from USDA/FooDB panel)
free glutamate (~1.5 mM) and free glutamine (~0.6 mM)
chloride, quantified fatty-acid profile, quantified pantothenate/choline/vitamins/minerals

curation_removed.name: Sucrose C12H22O11
curation_removed.reason: Mislabel/FooDB noise: human milk contains essentially no sucrose. The 6.9 g/100g carbohydrate is LACTOSE (glucose-galactose). Replaced by lactose as the dominant sugar.

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: Furanocoumarin from plants (Apiaceae/citrus); biologically implausible in human milk. FooDB predicted/expected noise, not a measured milk constituent.

basis: per 100 g fresh milk (density ~1.03 g/mL; per 100 g ~= per 97 mL)

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
